pages.title: About Pontotoc News
pages.excerpt: Learn about Pontotoc News, a Mississippi News Group publication covering Pontotoc County news, sports, weather and community life.
pages.content:
Pontotoc News covers news, sports and community life in Pontotoc, Mississippi, and Pontotoc County. Our aim is to give readers useful, clearly sourced information about the places where they live, work and go to school.

Our coverage

Local coverage comes first: schools, high school athletics, community events, public information and developments affecting Pontotoc County. We also publish Mississippi news, sports and weather updates that may matter to local readers. Statewide summaries are identified as statewide coverage; they should not imply that an event occurred in Pontotoc.

Our publisher

Pontotoc News is part of Mississippi News Group, a network of Mississippi news and sports publications. Jon Ross Myers, known professionally as Jon Myers, founded Mississippi News Group in 2013. Read his biography.

How our coverage is prepared

Our publishing includes source-based articles and summaries drawn from public agencies, schools, athletic programs, community organizations and other attributable sources. Some coverage uses AI-assisted research or writing and automated publishing. A published article should not be understood as a claim that a reporter attended the event or interviewed everyone mentioned. Our editorial standards explain sourcing, verification and the role of automation.

Send a news tip or correction

Have a story idea, announcement, photo or concern about an article? Use our contact form. Include relevant dates, locations, source links and a way to reach you. For an error, include the article URL and the information you believe needs correcting. See our corrections policy.

Businesses interested in supporting local coverage can use our advertising inquiry page.

Learn more: About Pontotoc News · Jon Myers · Editorial standards · Corrections · Contact us.

pages.title: Jon Myers
pages.excerpt: Meet Jon Myers, founder of Mississippi News Group, the network that includes Pontotoc News and local news and sports publications across Mississippi.
pages.content:
Jon Ross Myers, known professionally as Jon Myers, is the founder of Mississippi News Group. He founded the organization in 2013. Its network includes Pontotoc News and other publications covering Mississippi communities.

His publishing work spans local news and sports. He also founded Mississippi Sports Group, whose coverage focuses on Mississippi athletics.

Pontotoc News

Pontotoc News brings readers community news, sports and public information from Pontotoc County, along with relevant statewide coverage. His work connects local audiences with news and sports coverage across the Mississippi News Group network.

Readers can learn more about how coverage is prepared in our editorial standards, including our explanation of AI assistance and automated publishing.

Contact

For a Pontotoc news tip, question or correction request, use the Pontotoc News contact form. Include the article link when your message concerns published coverage, along with any source material that helps explain the issue.

Learn more: About Pontotoc News · Jon Myers · Editorial standards · Corrections · Contact us.

pages.title: Editorial Standards
pages.excerpt: Pontotoc News editorial standards for sourcing, accuracy, sports and weather reporting, AI-assisted publishing, attribution and corrections.
pages.content:
These standards guide coverage at Pontotoc News. Our goal is useful, accurate reporting and summaries that make clear what is known, where the information came from and what remains uncertain.

Sources and verification

We prioritize original, identifiable sources: public records, official announcements, schools, athletic programs, public agencies and people with direct knowledge. When coverage relies on another organization's announcement or reporting, the source should be named and linked when practical.

A social media post is a source to evaluate, not proof by itself. Names, dates, locations and the identity of the posting organization need checking. Information that cannot be supported should be left out or clearly described as unverified. Quotes must accurately reproduce an attributable source; invented quotes, events and statistics have no place in our coverage.

Local relevance and context

Articles should distinguish Pontotoc County developments from regional or statewide news. Headlines, summaries and images should accurately reflect the story. A summary should add useful organization and context rather than repeat unsupported claims or suggest reporting that did not occur.

Sports and weather

Sports coverage should verify the team, sport, game date and whether a score is final. Records, standings, player statistics and postseason implications need supporting sources. A score reported during a game should not be presented as a final result.

Weather coverage should identify the issuing agency and the time period covered by a forecast, warning or advisory. Old graphics and expired alerts should not be presented as current. Readers should consult the National Weather Service and local emergency officials for the latest safety instructions.

AI assistance and automated publishing

Pontotoc News uses AI-assisted tools and automation for parts of its publishing, including preparing source-based summaries. Some articles can publish through automated processes without a person reviewing each one beforehand. Automated checks are not a guarantee of accuracy. The publication remains responsible for addressing errors in its coverage.

AI output is not an independent source. The underlying information still needs support, and automated writing must not create quotations, people, statistics or events. Neither an automated summary nor an account byline should imply an interview or eyewitness reporting that did not happen.

Images, opinion and sponsored material

Images should be relevant, accurately described and used with appropriate permission or another valid basis. Illustrations, file photos and supplied images should not mislead readers about what was photographed or when. Opinion and paid or sponsored content should be clearly identified so readers can distinguish them from news coverage.

Corrections and reader feedback

Readers can flag a concern through our contact form. Our corrections policy explains what to include and how corrections differ from developing-story updates.

Learn more: About Pontotoc News · Jon Myers · Editorial standards · Corrections · Contact us.

pages.title: Corrections Policy
pages.excerpt: How to report an error to Pontotoc News and how factual corrections, clarifications and developing-story updates are handled.
pages.content:
Accuracy matters to Pontotoc News. Readers who believe an article contains an error can ask us to review it. This policy applies to reported articles, source summaries and AI-assisted or automatically published content.

How to request a correction

Use the Pontotoc News contact form. Begin your message with “Correction request” and include:

  • The article's title and URL.
  • The specific statement, name, date, score, image or other detail you believe is wrong.
  • The correct information, if known, and supporting links, records or other source material.
  • Your contact information so we can ask a follow-up question if necessary.

Please explain the factual issue as specifically as possible. A disagreement with a viewpoint is different from a factual error, but readers are welcome to send either concern.

Reviewing a request

Our standard is to compare the disputed information with the available evidence and relevant original sources. A request alone does not establish that an article is wrong. If the evidence is incomplete or conflicting, further checking may be needed before a change is made.

Corrections, clarifications and updates

A correction fixes information that was wrong when published. A clarification explains wording that was unclear or lacked important context. An update adds a later development to a story that was accurate at the time.

When a material factual error is confirmed, our standard is to correct the affected text and add a dated note explaining the substantive change. Minor spelling, punctuation or formatting fixes that do not change the meaning may be made without a separate note. Headlines, captions and summaries should be checked when they contain the same error.

New information should not be used to disguise an earlier mistake. If a story's central premise cannot be supported, an ordinary text edit may be insufficient; the appropriate response can include an editor's note or retraction explaining the problem.

Read our editorial standards for more on sourcing and automated publishing.

Learn more: About Pontotoc News · Jon Myers · Editorial standards · Corrections · Contact us.
